data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001's mechanism depends on the Swiss Cheese Model, where an error must pass through every checklist gate AND every panel member's verification. But this additive/independent-gates model can yield worse reliability than the expert on objectively-verifiable tasks with correlated gate failures: if a checklist item is ambiguously specified (as SRC_001's own countercondition 2 concedes is possible), panel members' verifications are no longer independent — a shared misreading propagates through all members at the same gate, collapsing the redundancy advantage. The target gives no account of how a single evaluation would detect this correlation structure versus genuine independent verification, which is precisely the evidential distinction the problem demands.
